column3: The Hebrew names Haman’s house; BSB calls it his estate.
The Hebrew separately names Haman’s evil and his plan; BSB combines them as his evil scheme.
The Hebrew says they hanged him and that he sent out his hand against the Jews; BSB uses a passive hanging clause and calls his action an attack.
The Hebrew says the scribes were summoned at that time and uses a passive writing clause; BSB says at once and makes the scribes the subject of recording.
The Hebrew leaves the writer unnamed in this verse; BSB explicitly names Mordecai.
The Hebrew continues with on one day; BSB supplies an independent statement about a single appointed day.
The Hebrew says the Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor; BSB adds a time of these things.
The Hebrew calls the celebration a good day; BSB renders this as celebrating.
